ansible-fundamentals-sr1-06.statement: With `ansible-pull`, each managed node checks out playbooks from Git and runs them on itself.
ansible-fundamentals-sr1-06.explanation: Pull mode reverses Ansible's default push model: a crontab on the node runs ansible-pull, which fetches the configuration and manages that machine locally.

Due to some string results previously parsing as lists, this mistake often went undetected", "The result of this template becomes a string", "entirely eliminating the final literal evaluation pass", plus the map('replace', ...) fix. ansible-fundamentals-sr7-11.statement: Since ansible-core 2.19, `{{ ['web1', 'web2'] | replace('web', 'db') }}` returns a string instead of a list.
ansible-fundamentals-sr7-11.explanation: replace works on strings, so it turns the list into text, and 2.19 removed the final literal-evaluation pass that used to parse such text back into a list. Use map('replace', ...) to keep a list.

ansible-fundamentals-sr12-11.statement: With DEFAULT_VAULT_ID_MATCH set, Ansible rejects a password that differs from one already used with the same vault ID.
ansible-fundamentals-sr12-11.explanation: Ansible does not tie a vault ID label to one password, even with DEFAULT_VAULT_ID_MATCH enabled, so two files can carry the same label with different passwords.
ansible-fundamentals-sr12-11.misconception: With DEFAULT_VAULT_ID_MATCH enabled, Ansible binds each vault ID label to a single password.
